commits.title: Publish builds stop sending product views to the Meta relay (Audit C01, build side)
commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes. The capture browser only runs while the site is being built.
commits.forMeta: Publish builds stop sending fake ViewContent events to the relay from 127.0.0.1 (the audit counted 154 per publish). I replayed the capture browser's own blocking rule on 3 product pages of the ddb72b7 build: the old rule let 3 of 3 relay posts through (event_source_url http://127.0.0.1:4470/jewellery/...), the shared pattern lets 0 through. Shopper events are unaffected.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged.
commits.risk: Low. This is git revert 63ed576, so e78c72b comes back exactly as it was. The capture browser still loads Shopify's catalogue, images, reels and fonts: the test checks that those addresses are allowed through. I did not run the prerender itself because the rules forbid it.

commits.title: Meta's server copy only reports from the real shop (Audit C01, app side)
commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes.
commits.forMeta: The server copy now follows the same gate as the browser pixel. Built page on 127.0.0.1: 1 relay post (ViewContent, event_source_url http://127.0.0.1:4470/...) before, 0 after. commits.title: Meta relay forwards only events from nairaflore.com pages (Audit C01, server side)
commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes.
commits.forMeta: Code only, not deployed. Once deployed, the relay forwards an event only when its page is https on nairaflore.com or www.nairaflore.com. Anything else gets 200 {skipped:"not_shop"} and nothing is sent to Meta. I ran the function's real source locally with Deno and Meta stubbed, using 18 test requests. Before, all 18 were forwarded. After, the 14 from shop pages are forwarded unchanged, and 4 are not: a Lovable preview, 127.0.0.1, a look-alike host, and a request with no page address.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged.
commits.risk: Low. The function now imports ./guard.ts from its own folder. If the shop ever serves pages on another host, the list in guard.ts has to be updated, the same as the __nairaProd allowlist.
commits.test: src/lib/metaCapiGuard.test.ts (15 tests: the host decision table, plus a check that the guard runs before the call to Meta). On ddb72b7 the suite cannot load because guard.ts does not exist; with the commit all 15 pass.

commits.title: Meta relay takes posts only from the shop's pages, and only the shop's events (Audit C14)
commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes. I checked the Origin header a shopper's browser actually sends: https://nairaflore.com from the apex and https://www.nairaflore.com from www, both allowed.
commits.forMeta: Code only, not deployed. Posts from any other Origin, or with no Origin, get 403 {error:"origin_not_allowed"}. Event names outside the 9 the pages send get 400 {error:"event_not_allowed"}. The 9 are ViewContent, AddToCart, AddToWishlist, InitiateCheckout, AddPaymentInfo, CompleteRegistration, Search, Lead and Contact; Purchase and made-up names are refused. I ran the function's real source locally on the 18 requests. Before C01 and C14, all 18 were forwarded. With both, the 10 genuine shop events are forwarded unchanged and the other 8 are not: 5 refused for their origin, 2 for their event name, 1 skipped for having no page address. SERVER_EVENTS in pixel.ts is now exported so a test keeps the two lists equal.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged.
commits.risk: Low. Adding a new server event in pixel.ts now also needs an entry in RELAYED_EVENTS, and a test fails until it has one. The Origin check stops other websites, but a script can fake the header; the event list and the page check are the real protection. I did not do the other hardening ideas in the finding (see skipped).
commits.test: src/lib/metaCapiGuard.test.ts. On the parent commit, 19 of 34 tests fail (the guard has no origin or event checks). With the commit, 34 of 34 pass.
commits.dependsOn: 2690b7c (Meta relay forwards only events from nairaflore.com pages).
commits.ownerQuestion: None needed to approve. If a new kind of event is ever added to the site, it must also be added to the relay's list (a test will remind whoever does it).

commits.ownerQuestion:
The duplicate 'checkout started' (InitiateCheckout) cannot be merged in code, because Shiprocket never sees our event id. Which one should Meta hear?
(a) Ours, sent at the Checkout tap. It covers both the Shiprocket and the Shopify checkout. You would switch off Shiprocket's InitiateCheckout in its Meta settings.
(b) Shiprocket's, sent on its own page. It carries the buyer's email and phone, so Meta matches it better, but it misses the Shopify fallback and anyone whose Shiprocket page fails to load. This needs a small code change on our side.
I recommend (a). The Fastrr plan also asked for ours to keep firing.

commits.title: fixup: Product views report the colour and size the page opens on (Audit C19)
commits.forShoppers: Nothing changes. The page, the colour it opens on, its price and what goes into the bag are the same. Only the moment the product view reaches Meta changes, on a few links.
commits.forMeta:
On the published site, product pages are pre-drawn with Shopify's own colours and sizes, so the C19 change already makes Star Point Band's Silver ad and Silver links name Silver US 6 at ₹799 there. This fix changes nothing for Star Point Band on the published site. It matters where a page's stored copy lacks the colour or item a link names. Measured on built pages, iPhone 13 and Pixel 7, landing cold, browser and server copy alike:
- Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet, with today's published pre-drawn page (made before White and Pink were added): the White ad, the Pink ad and the Pink link used to report Royal Blue (50714620100770). They now report White (50749309649058) or Pink (50749309681826), the colour on screen and in the bag, at the same ₹1,299. Each publish redraws the product pages from Shopify, so the publish that ships this also gives Aquarelle a pre-drawn page with White and Pink, and the C19 change alone then names them at once (measured). After that, this fix covers any colour or size added in Shopify after the latest publish, until the next one.
- A page opened without its pre-drawn copy (a preview, or a page the publish could not pre-draw): Star Point Band's Silver ad and Silver links go from Gold US 6 (47501788774562) at ₹999 to Silver US 6 (50652105605282) at ₹799. Its Gold link and its Gold US 5, 7 and 8 ads keep the Gold US 6 item, but its value goes from ₹999 to ₹799.
- A link naming a colour the piece is not sold in now waits for Shopify and reports Shopify's price. On the published site that price is already in the pre-drawn page, so only the timing changes (Molten Bloom Hoops ?colour=rose: ₹1,300 before and after, sent about half a second later). Without the pre-drawn copy, it went from ₹2,949 to ₹1,300.
- These views go out once Shopify answers: about 1 second after landing in the test (0.7 to 1.8 s), likely later on a slow phone connection. If Shopify has not answered within 3 seconds, the view goes out then, naming the stored item at the stored price, as before. If the shopper leaves, switches away or moves to another piece first, the view goes out at that moment.
- Still one product view per piece. Every other link sends it at once, as before.
commits.forCheckout: Unchanged. Measured on Pixel 7, ddb72b7, f7d43e9 and this commit alike. The Aquarelle White ad, on today's pre-drawn page: Add to cart puts White (50749309649058) x1 in the Shopify cart, and Buy Now hands Shiprocket White x1 with no code. The Star Point Band Silver ad, without its pre-drawn copy: Add to cart and Buy Now carry Silver US 6 (50652105605282) x1. The 'added to cart' and 'checkout started' events name the same item and price in all three builds (White ₹1,299, Silver ₹799).

commits.forShoppers: If the bag holds only that piece, and a shopper taps Add to cart and then Buy Now on it, checkout opens with 1 piece at full price. Before, it opened with 2 pieces at 15% off. The bag keeps 1. If the bag also holds other pieces, the piece now goes to checkout once, not twice. With the hoops and the bracelet in the bag: before, 3 pieces at 25% off; now, 2 pieces at 15% off. Buy Now on an empty bag, or on a piece the bag does not hold yet, works as before. Also changed: if the bag still shows the piece but Shopify no longer has it (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or the piece was taken out in another tab), Buy Now now opens checkout with the bag as it shows. Before, the bag was emptied with 'Your cart timed out' and 'Could not open checkout', and checkout did not open. (The fixup at the end, d8a943d, fixes this: Buy Now then puts the piece in again and opens checkout with it.)
commits.forMeta: Bracelet alone in the bag (2399): before, AddToCart fired twice (pixel and server each) and InitiateCheckout had value 4798, num_items 2. After, AddToCart fires once and InitiateCheckout has value 2399, num_items 1, content id 47501788348578. With the hoops also in the bag: one AddToCart fewer, and InitiateCheckout goes from value 6097, num_items 3 to 3698, num_items 2. When the Shopify cart is gone but the bag still shows the piece: before, no InitiateCheckout; now one (value 2399, num_items 1), from the pixel and the server. (With the fixup at the end, d8a943d, that case also sends one AddToCart, 2399, quantity 1, for the piece put back in.)
commits.forCheckout: Bracelet alone in the bag: Fastrr before got products [{47501788348578, qty 2}] with couponCode BUY2; after, [{47501788348578, qty 1}] with no coupon. With the hoops also in the bag: before, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,2}] with BUY3; after, [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2. The Shopify cart line is no longer raised to 2, and the extra rung code is no longer set. When Shopify no longer has the piece: before, nothing was handed off. Now Fastrr is handed the bag as it shows (Shopify cart gone: [{47501788348578, qty 1}], no coupon), but the Shopify checkout address it gets as its fallback points at a cart Shopify no longer has. With only the bracelet's line gone and the hoops also in the bag, Fastrr gets [{hoops,1},{bracelet,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart holds only the hoops. (The fixup at the end, d8a943d, fixes this: the piece is first put back on a Shopify cart that holds it.)
commits.risk: Low for the shop, but it changes money and Meta counts on this path: no second piece, no Buy 2 / Buy 3 code earned by that second piece, and one AddToCart fewer. Needs the owner's yes (the reviewer held it for that reason). On its own it also skips Shopify's check of that line (see above), so approve it together with the fixup d8a943d.

When Shopify has fewer left, AddToCart still reports the 2 asked for, although fewer were added. Main over-reports the same way, with 3.
commits.forCheckout: Measured with Blush of Dawn in S, in the bag once, 3 picked. Main gave Fastrr [{45794971222178, qty 4}] with BUY3. Now it gets [{45794971222178, qty 3}] with BUY3. commits.title: Bag Undo waits for an in-flight removal (restores 2128022)
commits.forShoppers: An Undo tapped straight after Remove brings the piece back, and the rest of the bag stays. Measured with Undo at 300 ms and the removal taking 900 ms. Before: if the Undo reached Shopify first, the hoops were silently lost; if the removal did, the whole bag was wiped as 'timed out'. Also changed, on a line Shopify no longer has (taken out in another tab, say): Remove now says 'Could not remove this item.' and keeps the row (the next commit, f2b05f4, fixes this). Tapping + says 'Could not update quantity.' and keeps the row. Adding that piece again says it couldn't be added, and the row stays (the fixup commit at the end, 5bbc08c, fixes these two). On main, all three emptied the whole bag; + and Add again also said 'Your cart timed out'. The row goes the next time the bag is opened.
commits.forMeta: Before: if the removal reached Shopify first, the Undo sent no AddToCart, because the add failed and the bag was wiped as 'timed out'. If the Undo reached Shopify first, it sent one AddToCart, for a piece that then vanished. After: the Undo always sends one AddToCart (hoops, 1299) from the pixel and from the server, for a piece that stays in the bag. Also, until f2b05f4 and 5bbc08c: after Remove or + on a line Shopify no longer has, the dead row stays, and the bag's Checkout then sends AddPaymentInfo (value 3143, num_items 2) and InitiateCheckout (value 3698, num_items 2) that count it, from the pixel and the server. On main the bag had been emptied, so neither was sent. Nothing else Meta receives changes.
commits.forCheckout: Shopify cart: before, Remove then 'set the removed line to 2' (or a refusal that wiped the bag); after, Remove then 'add the hoops', and the cart holds both. Checkout then gets what the bag shows (both pieces). Also: after Remove (until f2b05f4), or + or Add again (until 5bbc08c), on a line Shopify no longer has, checkout is still handed that dead row. Measured on this commit alone, applied to main: Fastrr got [{bracelet,1},{hoops,1}] with BUY2 while the Shopify cart held only the bracelet. On main the bag was emptied, so there was nothing to check out.
commits.risk: On its own it leaves the dead-line side effects described above. Approve it together with f2b05f4 (Remove) and the fixup 5bbc08c (+ and Add again), or say no to all three. Reverting the three together at the new head d8a943d is clean (676 tests pass, types check).

commits.title: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag first checks that Shopify still has it, and puts it back in if not
commits.forShoppers: This is for a piece still showing in the bag after Shopify has lost the bag (the Shopify cart ran out after some days, or was used for an order on Shopify's own checkout) or has dropped that piece (taken out in another tab, say). Buy Now on that piece now puts it in again and opens checkout with it, with no message. If Shopify lost the whole bag and the bag held other pieces too, those leave the bag, because Shopify no longer has them. If only that piece was dropped, the rest of the bag stays. On main the bag was emptied, 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.' and 'Your cart timed out. Please add the piece again.' showed, and checkout did not open. With 2b702d9 alone, checkout opened with the bag as it showed, on a Shopify cart that was gone. When Shopify still has the piece, checkout opens with the one piece already in the bag, as with 2b702d9, after one answer from Shopify (main waited for one answer here too; 2b702d9 alone skipped it).
commits.forMeta: Measured with Prism Riviere Bracelet (2399). When Shopify no longer has the piece, Buy Now now sends one AddToCart for it (value 2399, quantity 1, content id 47501788348578) from the Meta pixel and from the server, then InitiateCheckout (value 2399, num_items 1). On main neither was sent, because checkout did not open. 2b702d9 alone sent that InitiateCheckout but no AddToCart. commits.title: Bag lines take Shopify's current price on every cart answer
commits.ownerQuestion: Do you accept that the checkout value Meta receives (the checkout start and the payment step) follows Shopify's current price, not the price the page showed when the piece was added? The bag Total then always matches what you charge. Undo in the bag also puts a piece back at Shopify's price. Approve or decline together with 780534a, as one item.
commits.forShoppers: The bag's line prices, its Total and the Buy 2 / Buy 3 saving now always match what checkout charges. Before: a saved bag holding Mesh Band Ring at ₹699 showed ₹699 and a Total of ₹699, while Shopify charges ₹799. After: ₹799, Total ₹799. Heartline added from an out-of-date card at ₹2,449 showed ₹2,449 before and ₹1,899 after. Undo after removing a piece puts it back at ₹799 (it was ₹699). A signed-in member's account history also records Shopify's price for a started checkout. That last point comes from reading the code; it was not measured.
commits.forMeta: The checkout value Meta gets (InitiateCheckout) and its item price now follow Shopify's price, not the price the page showed at the tap. So does the payment-step value (AddPaymentInfo). The browser pixel and the server copy change together and still share one event id. Add to cart from a product page or card keeps the page's price. One exception: Undo after removing a piece in the bag re-adds it at the bag's price, which is now Shopify's. ViewContent is unchanged. Measured before → after: on the out-of-date bag, AddPaymentInfo 699→799 and InitiateCheckout value and item price 699→799. For Heartline, AddPaymentInfo 2449→1899 and InitiateCheckout 2449→1899, with Add to cart staying at 2449. Undo on the out-of-date bag sent Add to cart 699→799, browser pixel and server copy.
commits.forCheckout: No change. Shiprocket was handed the same pieces before and after: Mesh Band Ring (Gold, size 6) at quantity 1 and Heartline at quantity 1, with no code and the same fallback link. Shiprocket is never sent prices. The pieces in Shopify's cart do not change; Shopify is only read for its prices. In the Undo run nothing was handed over either way.
commits.risk: Low. If Shopify's answer has no price, the line keeps the price it has. The bag uses Shopify's price before discounts and works out the Buy 2 / Buy 3 saving itself. For Meta, three things change and the owner must accept them: the checkout value, the payment-step value and the Undo Add to cart. There are no Shopify Admin writes. The original commit message still says 'The Add to cart event keeps the page's price'. 780534a corrects that, and the folded message in fix-rev2/msgs/folded-c02.txt has the corrected text for packaging.
commits.test: src/contexts/bagPrices.test.tsx (4 cases: sync, add from an out-of-date card, quantity change, InitiateCheckout 699→799) and src/lib/cartLines.test.ts fail on ddb72b7 and pass here. src/components/bagUndoPrice.test.tsx, in 780534a, does too. With 780534a, applied alone on main, tsc passes and 650/650 tests pass (review run, and the F1 folded tree here).

commits.title: First paint shows Shopify's prices and sold-out state
commits.ownerQuestion: In the moment before the live catalogue arrives, prices, sold-out labels, photos and suggestions now follow today's Shopify. Do you accept that? That moment's ViewContent, Add to cart and checkout values to Meta then use today's prices. A sold-out piece then offers only Reserve now, or stops Buy Now with a message, instead of opening an empty checkout. Remember to re-run the price refresh whenever you reprice or restock. Approve or decline together with 0750c46 and cda5d47, as one item.
commits.forShoppers:
This covers the moment before the live catalogue arrives: about 0.5 s on fast wifi, 2 s or more on slow 4G. In that window, the 21 listing cards, the 'you may also like' rows and product pages reached inside the site now show today's Shopify price with MRP and % off. The five sold-out pieces read SOLD OUT with the button disabled instead of ADD TO CART. They also move to the end of the grid, so the order changes: Rivière Eternal Necklace goes from 2nd to 17th. Their own product pages, opened in that moment, now show only 'Reserve now' (the WhatsApp pre-order, 'Hand-finished for you and shipped within 2 weeks') instead of Add to cart and Buy Now, the same as once the catalogue arrives. Measured on Molten Bloom Hoops. Prices that change on first paint (old→new):
- Heartline 2449→1899 (MRP 3499)
- Bold Nocturne Chain 2449→1799 (4899)
- Serpentine Whisper Chain 1849→1299 (3359)
- Dewdrop Bezel 1299→999 (2599)
- Charm Box Chain 2149→1399 (3309)
- Molten Bloom Hoops 2949→1300 (2359), sold out
- Clover Trio Edit 2749→1999 (3929)
- Woven Gold Hoops 2349→1299 (2769)
- Ribbon Bow Earrings 2299→1199 (2000)
- Textured Gold Hoops 2849→1699 (3669)
- Solitaire Whisper Studs 1899→1099 (1900), sold out
- Rivière of Light Bracelet 1049→1249 (2269), sold out
- Bold Nocturne Bracelet 1999→1599 (3200)
- Baroque Bloom Cuff 1849→1499 (3079)
- Baguette Éclat Bracelet 1549→1699 (2769)
- Cushion Halo Ring 1499→1199 (2200)
- Chevron Whisper Ring 1449→1299 (2899)
- Star Point Band 999→799 (1500)
- First Light Set 1799→1199 (2909), sold out
- Rivière Eternal Necklace 1799 (unchanged), MRP 3269 added, sold out
- Pearl Ribbon Ring 1099 (unchanged), MRP 1600 added
- Mesh Band Ring 699→799 (all 8 sizes)
- Solitaire Drop Huggies 648→649 (MRP 1300)
- Roman Numeral Trio Ring sizes 7 and 9 now sold out
- Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet gains its White and Pink colours
In that moment, product pages reached inside the site also show Shopify's current photos and size-guide photos, about 50 pieces in all. For example, Baguette Tennis Necklace shows 8 photos instead of 11, Aquarelle Rivière Bracelet shows 13 instead of 6 with new wording, and Solitaire Drop Huggies gets its size-guide photo. Their 'Complete the look' and 'More …' rows no longer suggest the sold-out pieces. Some rows also swap one in-stock piece for another or change order. Woven Gold Hoops now suggests Serpentine Whisper Chain instead of Charm Box Chain. Roman Numeral Trio Ring now suggests Bold Nocturne Chain and Bold Nocturne Bracelet instead of Serpentine Whisper Chain and Baguette Éclat Bracelet. These rows still come only from the 21 bundled pieces, so they still differ from the rows shown once the catalogue arrives. A piece added in that moment goes into the bag at today's price (Woven Gold Hoops ₹2,349 before, ₹1,299 after). A piece Shopify has just sold out no longer lands in the bag as '₹2,349 × 0, Total ₹0'. The bag now says 'Woven Gold Hoops couldn't be added. It may have just sold out.' The listing still swaps 30 prebuilt cards for 21 bundled ones; that layout part is not fixed here.
commits.forMeta: ViewContent and Add to cart values for a piece seen or added before the catalogue arrives carry the new prices. Measured on the Woven Gold Hoops page: ViewContent 2349→1299 and Add to cart 2349→1299, browser and server copy alike. The bag keeps the price of a piece added in that moment, so its payment-step and checkout values follow too, even without C02. Measured with Heartline added from its card: AddPaymentInfo 2449→1899 and InitiateCheckout value and item price 2449→1899. An add Shopify answers with 0 (sold out) no longer sends Add to cart. Measured: before, Add to cart 2349 was sent; after, none. Buy Now on a sold-out ring under main's adjustable rule: before, Add to cart 1599 and InitiateCheckout (no value, 0 pieces) were sent; after, neither is sent. The five sold-out pieces' own pages, opened in that moment, now offer only Reserve now, which sends nothing to Meta. Before, their Buy Now sent Add to cart at the old price and InitiateCheckout with 0 pieces. Measured on Molten Bloom Hoops: Add to cart 2949 and InitiateCheckout before, none after. Its ViewContent went 2949→1300. Each event's browser pixel and server copy still share one event id.
commits.forCheckout: A piece Shopify answers at 0 (sold out) is no longer handed to Shiprocket. Measured: Buy Now on a sold-out ring under main's adjustable rule handed Shiprocket the ring at quantity 0 before. After, there is no hand-off and the shopper sees 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.' and 'couldn't be added'. On the five sold-out pieces' own pages opened in that moment, Buy Now used to hand Shiprocket the piece at quantity 0 (measured on Molten Bloom Hoops). Now the page shows only Reserve now, which opens the WhatsApp pre-order message ('Molten Bloom Hoops (₹1,300)'), and nothing is handed to Shiprocket. Checkout of anything Shopify can sell is unchanged: Heartline was handed over at quantity 1, no code, both times.
commits.risk: Low to medium. The bundled data is a dated copy of Shopify. It goes stale again until the refresh is re-run, and the live catalogue still corrects it within the visit. A line of 0 is refused only after the right size's line is picked, so one size never borrows another size's line, and the commit does not need C02 underneath it. The data was checked read-only against the live store at 23:35 on 30 Oct and again at 00:54 on 31 Oct. Every bundled price, MRP, stock flag and variant matched. Tubogas Dome Ring's Silver photos still show the Gold photo in Shopify, so its earlier entry is kept. By 01:00 on 31 Oct Shopify had two new pieces the bundle does not hold. The first-paint suggestion rows still come only from the 21 bundled pieces. The original commit message leaves out the grid order, photos, rows, payment-step values and the sold-out product pages. The folded message in fix-rev2/msgs/folded-c25.txt has all of them for packaging.

commits.title: Add to cart tells Meta only what Shopify really added
commits.ownerQuestion: Is it OK to stop telling Meta about Add to cart taps that added nothing because the last piece was already in the bag, and to count 1 instead of 2 when only 1 more could be added?
commits.forShoppers: No visible change. The bag still keeps 1 and says 'Only 1 of Woven Gold Hoops left, all in your bag'. Buy Now still goes to checkout with the bag as it is.
commits.forMeta: Add to cart is sent only for the pieces Shopify really added, with that quantity and its value. The count is the bag line's quantity after the add, less what the bag held before, and never more than was asked for. The event id and the server copy work as before. Measured with 1 piece left (Add, Add again, Buy Now): before, 3 Add to cart events of 1,299 each (browser pixel and server copy); after, 1. With a piece Shopify answers at 0 (Buy Now on a sold-out ring, this commit alone): before, Add to cart 1,599; after, none. With C25 approved, such a line is refused one step earlier as 'couldn't be added', and the two never both act on one add.
commits.forCheckout: No change. The checkout start (1,299, 1 piece) and the hand-off to Shiprocket (Woven Gold Hoops at quantity 1, no code) were identical before and after. On its own, this commit still lets Buy Now hand a sold-out piece over at quantity 0; C25 is what stops that.
commits.risk: Low. Only when Add to cart is sent, and with what quantity, changes. What the bag does and how Buy Now runs are unchanged. The Add to cart value still uses the price the tap carried: the page's price, or the bag line's price for Undo.
commits.test: src/contexts/addToCartCount.test.tsx has 5 cases: a capped existing line, a part-filled line, a capped new cart, a line of 0 and a full add. 4 fail on ddb72b7 and all pass here. Applied alone on main: tsc passes and 648/648 tests pass.

commits.title: Raising a piece's quantity in the bag counts as an Add to cart
commits.ownerQuestion: Is it OK for '+' in the bag to count as an Add to cart for Meta, one per piece added?
commits.forShoppers: No visible change.
commits.forMeta: Each '+' in the bag that Shopify accepts now sends one Add to cart for the pieces really added (1 for a '+'), at the bag line's price. It goes the same way as every other Add to cart, so the browser pixel and the server copy share one event id. A '+' that Shopify caps at its stock sends nothing, and so does any '−'. Measured with Add, '+' to 2, '+' to 3 (Shopify keeps 2), '−' to 1, then Checkout. Before, 1 Add to cart in all. After, 2: the second was quantity 1, value 1,299, with the same event id on the pixel and the server copy. The line price is the page's price at the add, or Shopify's price if C02 is approved.
commits.forCheckout: No change. AddPaymentInfo, the checkout start (1,299, 1 piece) and the hand-off to Shiprocket (Woven Gold Hoops at quantity 1) were identical.
commits.risk: Low. The count is capped at the raise asked for, so an out-of-date bag line cannot over-count. It does not double count with a normal Add, which goes its own way.
commits.test: src/contexts/bagRaise.test.tsx has 3 cases. The '+' case fails on ddb72b7. The capped '+' and the '−' pass before and after, as guards. All pass here. Applied alone on main: tsc passes and 646/646 tests pass.

commits.ownerQuestion: When an adjustable ring sells out in Shopify, which do you want? (A) Keep the site as it is: Add to cart and Buy Now stay on its page and in reels. Buy Now then cannot complete: today it opens an empty checkout, and with C25 it shows 'Could not open checkout'. (B) Switch it to 'Reserve now' on WhatsApp like every other sold-out piece, with no Buy Now. Approve or decline together with 89076f1, as one item.
commits.forShoppers:
This matters only once Shopify marks an adjustable ring sold out. Read-only checks at 23:55 on 30 Oct and 01:17 on 31 Oct found all 14 in stock. Measured with Rose Verdant Band set to sold out in Shopify's answer:
- On main, the page shows Add to cart, Buy Now and 'US 6 ships now…'.
- With this commit, the page shows only 'Reserve now', with 'Hand-finished for you and shipped within 2 weeks, gift-boxed'. Reserve opens the WhatsApp pre-order message with the ring, its size and price.
- Rose Verdant Band is in no reel, so the reel lists looked the same on both builds.
- In a separate run, Cushion Halo Ring (the one adjustable ring in a reel) was set to sold out. Its reel row went from '₹1,199 Add' to 'Pre-order Reserve'. A reel row changes only when its own ring is sold out. Cushion Halo has about 60 in stock, so approving this changes no reel today.
- With the rings in stock, both builds are identical.
commits.forMeta: With this commit, no Add to cart or checkout start is sent for a sold-out adjustable ring, because no checkout starts. On main the same Buy Now sends Add to cart 1,599 and a checkout start (InitiateCheckout) with no value and 0 pieces. With C25 also approved, main's Buy Now sends neither.
commits.forCheckout:
The choice, and what each does to Buy Now:
- Keep the site as it is (do not approve). Since the 30 Sep product page, Buy Now stays on a ring Shopify has sold out. The owner's 25 Oct note, that every adjustable ring fits US 5 to 9, was about sizes and did not set this. As main stands, Buy Now opens Shiprocket with the ring at quantity 0. With C25, it stops with 'Could not open checkout. Please try again.'
- Follow Shopify (approve). Reserve now (WhatsApp) replaces Buy Now and nothing is handed to Shiprocket. Google is told out of stock instead of in stock.
commits.risk: Owner decision, and nothing changes today (no adjustable ring is sold out). The original commit message misdates the rule to 25 Oct and puts the Cushion Halo reel result in the Rose Verdant run. 89076f1 corrects both, and the folded message in fix-rev2/msgs/folded-c27.txt has the corrected text for packaging.
